3600:
** ὀδῠν-άω**,
_aorist_ ὀδυνῆσαι {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 10.853}}:—_passive_, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ παρρησίας” p.29}} O.; _2nd pers._ _singular_ ὀδυνᾶσαι {{NT|NT.Luke.16.25}}: _future_ ὀδυνηθήσομαι {{Refs 4th c.BC+|2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 10.851, but ὀδυνήσομαι 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 325.16, 3rd c.BC: Teles Philosophus “fragment” 2p.9 H}}.: _aorist_ ὠδυνήθην {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 3}}:— **cause** one **pain** or **suffering,** τὸ γὰρ ὀρθοῦσθαι γνώμαν ὀδυνᾷ {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 247 (_anapaest meter_), compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 164; οὐ τοὐμὸν ὀδυνήσει σε γῆρας [prev. author] “Ec.” 928; μηδὲν ὀδύνα τὸν πατέρα 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 659}}:—_passive_, **feel pain, suffer pain,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 159, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 4.12, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 804, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 283, “Ra.” 650, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 583d, etc.; ἃ ὠδυνήθην}}**the pains I suffered,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 3, compare 9}}; _Ionic dialectpresent_ **ὀδυνέομαι** {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “περὶ αἰτιῶν καὶ σημείων χρονίων παθῶν” 2.4.}}

3647:
** ὁλοκληρ-ία**, ἡ,
**completeness** or **soundness in all parts,** τοῦ σώματος, τῶν αἰσθητηρίων, {{NT+4th c.BC+|3rd c.BC: Chrysippus Stoicus 3.33, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1041f: _absolutely_, NT.Act.3.16, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1063f, 4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 3, “SIG” 1142 (Phrygia, 1st-2nd c.AD), “POxy.” 123.6 (3rd-4th c.AD).}}
3648:
** ὁλόκληρ-ος**, ον,
**complete, entire, perfect,** opposed to κολοβός, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 585b36}}; **uncastrated,** κίχλαι {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 174.9; τοὺς ἱερέας ὁ. νόμος εἶναι 4th c.BC: Anaxandrides Comicus 39.10, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 233, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Asin.” 33; ὁ. ὑγιής τε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 44c; σῶμα 2nd c.AD: Diogenes Oenoandensis Epicureus 39; ὁ. μὲν.. ὄντες καὶ ἀπαθεῖς κακῶν.., ὁ. δὲ.. καὶ εὐδαίμονα φάσματα μυούμενοι}}**perfect, complete,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 250c; ὁ. καὶ γνήσιον [prev. author] “Lg.” 759c; ἐν ὁ. δέρματι 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Philops.” 8}}; also of evils, ὁ. πήρωσις {{Refs 4th c.BC+|3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 296; [ἡ ἀνελευθερία] οὐ πᾶσιν ὁ. παραγίνεται 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1121b19, compare 1126a12}}; simply, **whole, complete,** ἔτεσιν δυσὶν οὐχ ὁλοκλήρ[οι]ς {{Refs 4th c.AD+|“IG” 14.1386; ὁ. βουλευτήριον “BGU” 1027.12 (4th c.AD)}}; ὁ. οἰκία {{Refs|“PLond.” 3.930.13, etc.}}; ὁ. κολλούρια drug-pencils used **as wholes,** for insertion in cavities, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Antyllus Medicus cited in 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 10.23.1}}. _adverb_ **-ρως**[{{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st c.AD: Erotianus Grammaticus see {ἀπαρτί}, 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “Πυρρώνειοι ὑποτυπώσεις” 3.226, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 16.68, 3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 7.8.}}]
3649:
** ὀλολύζω**,
{{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.411, etc.}}: _future_ **-ύξομαι**{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 691}}, later **-ύξω** {{LXX|LXX.Isa.16.7, LXX.Amos.8.3:}}_aorist_ ὠλόλυξα, _Epic dialect_ ὀ. (see. below):—**cry with a loud voice,** in {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus}} especially of women **crying aloud** to the gods in prayer or thanksgiving, ὣς εἰποῦσ᾽ ὀλόλυξε· θεὰ δέ οἱ ἔκλυεν ἀρῆς {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.767, compare “hymnus ad Apollinem” 445}}; αἱ δ᾽ ὀλόλυξαν, at a sacrifice, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.450}}; of a cry of exultation, ἴθυσέν ῥ᾽ ὀλολύξαι {{Refs|22.408, compare 411}}; also of the cries of goddesses, {{Refs|“hymnus ad Apollinem” 119}}; so later, mostly of women **crying** to the gods, ὀλολύξατε νῦν ἐπὶ μολπαῖς {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 1043 (Lyric poetry); ὠλόλυξεν ἐν μέσαις σταθεῖσα Βάκχαις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 689}}; mostly in sign of joy (compare ὀλολυγή), ἢν μὲν ἔλθῃ πύστις εὐτυχὴς σέθεν, ὀλολύξεται πᾶν δῶμα {{Refs 5th c.BC+|[prev. author] “El.” 691, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1327, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 17.64; μὴ φλαῦρον μηδὲν γρύζειν, ἀλλ᾽ ὀ. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 97; ἐπὶ τῷ μηδένα πώποτε τηλικοῦτ᾽ ὀλολύξαι σεμνυνόμενος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.259; ὠλόλυξαν μὲν αἱ γυναῖκες, ἠλάλαξαν δὲ οἱ ἄνδρες 3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 3.5}}; of nymphs **crying aloud** to Hecate, {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.1218.}}

3665:
** ὁμοιό-της**, ητος, ἡ,
**likeness, resemblance,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 164, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 109a, +others: _plural_, [prev. work] 82a, “Sph.” 231a}}; ἡ αὑτοῖς ὁ. τῆς διαγωγῆς **mode** of passing life **like** themselves, {{Refs|[prev. author] “Tht.” 177a}}; ὁμοιότητι τετάχθαι κατά τι **correspond** to.., {{Refs|[prev. author] “R.” 555a}}; so ὁμοιότητι εἶναι κατά τι{{Refs|[prev. work] 576c; ὁμοιότητι}}**equally,** {{Refs|[prev. author] “Ti.” 75d}}: with _dative_, **resemblance to..,** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|[prev. author] “Phdr.” 253b, +others; [ὁμοιότητες] γίνονται τοῖς τέκνοις πρὸς τοὺς γεννήσαντας 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1262a16, compare “EN” 1108b31}}; τίνι τῶν ζῴων εἰς ὁμοιότητ; in **likeness** of what animal ? {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 30c, compare 81d}}; καθ᾽ ὁμοιότητα λέγεσθαι, opposed to ἁπλῶς, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1147b34}}; καθ᾽ ὁ. σημειοῦσθαι, ἡ καθ᾽ ὁ. σημείωσις, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ σημείων καὶ σημειώσεων” 31, 34; ὁ κατὰ τὴν ὁ. τρόπος [prev. work] 8}}; later καθ᾽ ὁμοιότητα with _genitive_, **in the same way as,** ἀξιῶν ἐνταγῆναι κἀμοῦ τὸν υἱὸν τῇ τῶν ἐφήβων γραφῇ καθ᾽ ὁ. τῶν σὺν αὐτῷ {{NT+2nd c.AD+|“POxy.” 1202.24 (3rd c.AD), compare 237 vi6 (2nd c.AD), “BGU” 1028.15 (2nd c.AD), “PSI” 1.107.2 (2nd c.AD), NT.Heb.7.15: without _genitive_, [prev. work] 4.15.}}
3667:

3689:
** ὄντως**,
_adverb_ _participle_ of εἰμί **(sum), really, actually, verily,** with Verbs, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 610, “Ion” 223 (Lyric poetry), “IA” [1622], 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 86, “Pl.” 286, 289, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 4.65, etc.}}; ὄντως τε καὶ ἀληθῶς **really** and truly, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 263d; ὄ. φιλοσοφεῖν 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 220}}; opposed to to ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 656e}}; to εἰκότως, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.2.10 and 4.10: in 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus with the}}_participle_ ὤν, οὖσα, ὄν, to imply **real** existence, {{Refs|“Phdr.” 247c, 247e, “R.” 597d}}: also with Nouns, τὰ ὄντως ἀγαθά {{Refs 5th c.BC+|[prev. author] “Phdr.” 260a; ὅ γε ὄντως φιλομαθής [prev. author] “R.” 490a; ὄντως ἑταίρας 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 212.6, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 367, etc.: not used by 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus or 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus, nor in _Ionic dialect_ (ἐόντως is not found)}}; more freq in the later dialogues of {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus than in the earlier.}}
